title: threshold
content_html:
threshold

In the Moment boundary conditions, the room can be described with certainty while time slips its usual frame. Boundary conditions (by the river) gives the idea another setting. A threshold is a place we might stand in and a point at which something starts to happen. The first recognition of a figure and the onset of an unbidden recollection each have a threshold of their own. Can we locate the crossing while it happens, or does it become visible only afterwards? Boundary conditions (by the river) · boundary conditions · Spontaneous Recall Seems Random

Reading note. Alchemy and Jung. Jung’s discussion of nigredo, or blackening, describes it as a starting condition in some accounts and an effect of separation in others. Can we locate the beginning of a change by looking at what preceded it, or does a later state let us recognise where the threshold was? Psychology and Alchemy, §334
